name: Deepavali Lamps & Rangoli
summary: Twelve clay diyas, a round geometric rangoli and two hanging marigold garlands.
description: Original twelve-diya display with wide ivory-and-gold static flames, an included 2 x 2 m chamfered clay floor, a ground-supported 2.4 m round three-colour geometric rangoli, and two supported marigold garlands of 21 layered flower heads each. Hollow clay bowls, wicks and a freestanding two-post frame on clear rear-corner feet; no text, brands, religious figures or external assets.
author: Yap Wei Jun project / Codex-assisted procedural modeling
creation_method: Original deterministic Blender Python; three plain shared materials; no external models, images, textures, fonts or scripts.
accuracy_notes: Measured export dimensions are X width, Y height, Z depth. The included 2 x 2 m chamfered square floor spans X/Z [-1, 1], from Y=0 to 0.012 m. The 2.4 m mosaic has an 8 mm top layer at Y=0.012 to 0.020 m; its four exterior circular caps extend to Y=0 without overlapping the square-floor volume. Matching terracotta surfaces and 40 mm corner chamfers form a continuous ground base. All twelve lamps fit inside the square and rest at Y=0.020 m. Support feet centred at X=+/-0.93 m, Z=-0.93 m are fully supported, with measured radial clearance of 64.99 mm from the 1.2 m rangoli radius and 18.00 mm from the square-floor edges. Posts, crossbar and four garland loops share the same rear depth. Place the origin on level ground at Y=0. Flames are static meshes without emitted lights or simulation. Physical devices, WebKit and full-mall performance are not verified.

attribution.credit: Original procedural geometry and materials created for the owner project. No third-party assets.

rights: Original asset; reuse in the owner's projects is authorized. Public redistribution terms have not been specified.
material_notes: Three shared opaque materials and three delivery meshes. Terracotta: ground base, bowls, wicks and support frame; MarigoldGold: layered flower heads, oil and flame cores; RiceIvory: flame bodies, hangers and mosaic accents. The closed stepped rangoli has no coplanar overlays or volume overlap with the square floor.
